abstract: The mechanism controlling the dynamic targeting of SWI/SNF has long been postulated to be coordinated by transcription factors (TFs), yet demonstrating specific TF influence has proven difficult. In this study we take a multi-omics approach to interrogate transient SWI/SNF interactors, chromatin targeting, and the resulting 3D epigenetic landscape. We utilized the labeling technique TurboID to map the SWI/SNF interactome, and identified the AP-1 family members as critical interacting partners for SWI/SNF complexes. CUT&RUN profiling demonstrated SWI/SNF targeting enrichment at AP-1 bound loci, and SWI/SNF – AP-1 cooperation in chromatin targeting. HiChIP revealed AP-1-SWI/SNF dependent restructuring of 3D promoter-enhancer architecture and generation of enhancer hubs. Through interrogation of the SWI/SNF – AP-1 interaction, we demonstrate a SWI/SNF dependency on AP-1-mediated chromatin localization. We propose that pioneer factors, such as AP-1, bind and target SWI/SNF to inactive chromatin, where it restructures the genomic landscape into an active state through epigenetic rewiring spanning multiple dimensions.
